summary: ASTERIA is a web tool for planning lunar south pole landings. For a candidate site and date, it shows when the site has sunlight and a direct line of sight to Earth, using NASA LOLA terrain data and an ephemeris validated against NASA JPL Horizons. Planners can compare sites, see how a launch delay changes conditions, estimate solar power, check mission requirements, print a sourced Mission Casefile, and explore the real terrain in 3D near eight candidate sites.
details:
What it does: Lunar south pole landing sites have sunlight and Earth visibility only part of the time, because the Sun skims the horizon and mountains block it. ASTERIA answers, for a site and time window: when is the Sun up, when is Earth visible, when are both, how long is the longest darkness or communications blackout, and what happens if the launch slips. It also estimates solar energy and battery needs, checks user-defined mission requirements (Met / Not met / Can't assess, with no hidden scores), and produces a printable Mission Casefile.

How it works: Sun and Earth positions come from Astronomy Engine with the IAU Moon orientation. Terrain horizons are ray-traced over NASA LRO/LOLA elevation models (5 m to 120 m grids) in 360 directions to 300 km, including lunar curvature, for an observer 2 m above the ground. A clicked point gets a terrain horizon from a validated 240 m grid. The 3D view renders the real LOLA terrain for points near the eight candidate sites.

Validation: Sun and Earth elevation angles match NASA JPL Horizons to within 0.004 degrees, rise and set times to within 1.5 minutes over a full year, and 336 out of 336 independent sunlit/visible decisions agree. Average illumination is about 2 percentage points from NASA PGDA maps, and 14.5 million 3D terrain points are within 0.1 m of the source data. A Validation page and a "Verify with NASA" link let anyone reproduce the checks.

Historical Capsule: a short illustrated animation of space-exploration milestones from Sputnik to Artemis, with every caption sourced from NASA, ISRO and JAXA pages. It is kept separate from the science and labelled "not ASTERIA data".

Tools: JavaScript, Leaflet, Three.js, Python for data processing, Playwright for automated testing, and GitHub Pages for hosting. Source code: https://github.com/ASTERIA-LUNAR/asteria. The project was developed under human direction with assistance from Claude Code (Anthropic), an AI coding assistant; details are in AI_DISCLOSURE.md in the repository.
